analogies.summary: This study describes a solid acid catalyzed liquid-phase aromatic nitration reaction using concentrated nitric acid in a continuous flow system. The reaction was conducted at 120°C in dichloroethane (DCE) solvent at 1.0 M concentration using a packed-bed reactor with a volume of 7.85 mL and a flow rate of 0.91 mL/min. The flow process achieved 90% yield compared to 92% yield in the corresponding batch reaction conducted under similar conditions (120°C, 1 hour reaction time). analogies.summary: A photochemical cyclization reaction proceeding through a nitrene intermediate mechanism was conducted using 465 nm blue LEDs in acetonitrile solvent at 25°C and 0.1 M concentration. The continuous-flow photoreactor operated with a 10-minute residence time and 0.1 mL/min flow rate, achieving a 65% yield without requiring a photocatalyst. In comparison to the batch process, which required 10 hours (600 minutes) and only achieved 55% yield, the flow setup delivered a remarkable 60-fold reduction in reaction time while improving yield by 18.2%. The flow advantage stems from superior light intensity control and more efficient photon delivery in the continuous reactor design. This represents a significant process intensification with both time and yield benefits for the nitrene-mediated cyclization.
